stories.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
stories.what: Tankers have been attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz, including explosives attached to a hull, and strikes on commercial vessels continue amid threats of renewed US action against Iran.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on hulls raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Hormuz transits, shrinking the pool of owners willing to lift Arabian Gulf cargoes and supporting crude tanker earnings.
stories.latest: gCaptain reported on 31 October that the strikes are inflicting economic pain on both sides as renewed attacks are threatened; trade press also describes Gulf crude moving around the strait.
sources: Shipping Strikes In Hormuz Leave Both Sides With Economic Pain
Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?

stories.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
stories.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea this month.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Dockworkers Strike Continues Friday Against Arms Shipments

stories.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
stories.what: Hormuz recorded six VLCC transits on Oct 25, the most since Oct 17, with one VLCC through Bab al-Mandab on each of Oct 24 and Oct 25. Vessel waiting remains elevated across the Arabian Gulf, with 265 dry bulk vessels waiting as of 28 October and Fujairah holding 28% of them.
stories.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
stories.latest: Trade press notes Gulf crude continuing to move around the strait as China's stockpile cushion draws down.
sources: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia's government has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
stories.latest: Russia extended its diesel export ban through January, reported 31 October.
sources: Russia Extends Ban On Most Diesel Exports Through January

stories.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
stories.what: A contract standoff involving 250 security workers threatens to freeze operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals after a 4 November deadline extension, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond on Friday over arms shipments through their ports.
stories.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.
stories.latest: The LA-Long Beach dispute now centres on 250 security workers with a 4 November deadline extension.
sources: Impending strike threatens LA-LB ports container flow
Dockworkers Strike Continues Friday Against Arms Shipments

stories.title: Chinese patrols off Taiwan's east coast
stories.what: Taiwan's Coast Guard says China's Coast Guard is harassing shipping with a patrol off Taiwan's east coast and asserting what Taipei calls a fictional jurisdiction, and has sent its own ships in response.
stories.why_it_matters: Interference with commercial traffic near a major East Asian routing corridor can affect transit decisions, insurance and schedules for ships serving North Asia.
stories.latest: Taiwan publicly accused China's Coast Guard of harassing shipping on 1 November.
sources: Taiwan Says China Harassing Shipping With East Coast Patrol
